title: A user function is described in five places and typed in none of them
author: Claude-JG
description: Traced 2026-09-25 for ObjectGenericODE2.forceUserFunction. The same signature is stated in the ItemParameter's type (TPyFunctionVectorMbsScalarIndex2Vector), in the std::function that definitionTypes maps it to, in the prose block of the item description with its own argument table, in the generated userFunctionArgsDict of itemInterface.py, and in the hand-written call in evaluateUserFunctions.cpp. Nothing checks that the five agree, and the one a user could actually use is the weakest: userFunctionArgsDict names the arguments arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3 and types them with the C++ names (StdVector, Real, Index), which is what advancedUtilities builds the symbolic function interface from. The registry the maintainer asked for therefore already exists and is only half filled in. Proposal (maintainer 2026-09-25, from a design discussed the same day): one typed Python function per user function in the ItemDefinition, parsed with ast and never executed, as the single source of the argument names, the Python types, the per-argument description - where the size of an argument is a formula in the description rather than part of the type - the documentation block, the entries of userFunctionArgsDict, and a Protocol per user function in itemInterface so that an editor can complete and check a user function's arguments. 23 distinct signatures under 17 names, in 35 blocks; to be tried on one function first.
workingRemarks: revision2026b step RG12.4.2 done: ObjectGround.graphicsDataUserFunction is a real Python def in definitions/itemDefsObjects.py; the documentation block is generated from its annotations and docstring, and the generated page is unchanged apart from one blank line that sat inside the example's code fence. userFunctionArgsDict carries the real argument names, and the number of arguments is checked against the std::function of the parameter's type. The rules are in definitions/README.md, section 'Writing a description'. 1 of 23 signatures converted.; revision2026b step RG12.4.3 done: userFunctionModel.CheckAgainstCpp compares the Python def with the std::function of the parameter's type - the number of arguments, each argument's type, the return type, and that the docstring describes every argument. A size is not compared, because a size belongs in the description and not in the type. itemInterfaceEmitter raises on a finding, tools/checkDefinitions.py reports it with the file and the line.; revision2026b step RG12.4.4 done: itemInterface.py carries a Protocol per user function written as a def - class ObjectGroundGraphicsDataUserFunction(Protocol) with a typed __call__ and the docstring - and the item parameter is annotated Union[Protocol, int], because 0 means no user function. parameterConversionTest.py had to skip a class whose _is_protocol is true: it creates every class of the module whose name starts with an item kind.; revision2026b step RG12.4.5.1 done: the vocabulary of sizes - Vector3D/Vector6D/Matrix3D/Array as annotations, a size that is not fixed as the leading $\in ...$ of the argument's description - and the four loads plus SensorUserFunction converted, six user functions of 23. RG12.4.7 filed: the TPyFunction group types can be eliminated, because cppToAnnotation is now one to one.; revision2026b step RG12.4.5.2 done: eight connector items, ten user functions, 16 of 23. Two signatures were wrong and the conversion found them - CoordinateSpringDamper advertised dryFriction and dryFrictionProportionalZone, removed in 2023-01-21 (V1.5.76), and CoordinateSpringDamperExt broke its fourteen-argument signature over two lines. ObjectConnectorRigidBodySpringDamper is left for RG12.4.5.3: its postNewtonStep block says 'other arguments see springForceTorqueUserFunction' instead of listing them, writes 'Index itemIndex' in a Python signature, and types stiffness and damping as Vector6D where the C++ takes a 6x6 matrix.; revision2026b steps RG12.4.5.3, .5.4 and .6 done: all 34 user functions are Python defs, a gate reports any parameter without one, and userFunctionArgsDict carries the Protocol name so that the ConvertFunctionToSymbolic error points at it. Four more documentation errors found and fixed: postNewtonStepUserFunction wrote 'Index itemIndex' and listed four of thirteen arguments, stiffness/damping were typed Vector6D where the C++ takes a 6x6 matrix, ObjectJointGeneric typed a 6D offset vector as Real, and ObjectRigidBody2D wrote int for itemNumber.
